episodes.label: evidence-sft-r2-paired-literal-write-repair-r1-baseline-city-shade
episodes.notes: [chapter-p001] In a fictional study of summer heat in Bellwick, researchers compared twelve streets with mature trees and twelve nearby streets without them. Sensors recorded air temperature at pedestrian height between noon and six in the evening on ten dry days. The shaded streets were cooler on average, but the difference was largest late in the afternoon. These measurements describe the sampled streets and weather; they do not establish how much planting a new tree would immediately cool another neighborhood.

[exceptions-p01] Ticket-system outage: agents keep offline log with ticket identifiers and timestamps; after recovery, import log without overwriting newer activity.
[exceptions-p02] Suspected duplicates: mark as related; retain both records until reviewer decides whether merge is safe.
[exceptions-p03] Weekly review: compare ticket-system counts with offline-log counts; any difference remains explicitly unresolved until cause documented.
[exceptions-p04] Support lead approval: approve routine corrections; delete record or change customer-visible deadline requires approval from operations manager.

episodes.label: evidence-sft-r2-paired-literal-write-repair-r1-candidate-city-shade
episodes.notes:
[chapter-p001] Twelve streets with mature trees measured against twelve without; sensors recorded pedestrian-height air temperature between noon and six on ten dry days. Shaded streets cooler on average, but difference largest late afternoon; measurements describe sampled streets and weather, not how much planting immediately cools another neighborhood.
[chapter-p002] Shade reduces pavement and people's sunlight absorption; trees release water vapor through leaves, cooling surrounding air. Mechanisms related but not interchangeable: awning provides shade without water release, tree with sparse foliage releases water without much sun shelter. Study did not separately measure contribution of either mechanism.
[chapter-p003] Tree cover unevenly distributed; older residential streets wider planting strips and more mature canopies, several shopping streets narrow sidewalks and dense underground utilities. Hottest blocks contained busiest bus stops; counting trees across entire district concealed differences in where people waited or walked; authors suggested measuring shade along common routes, not merely reporting district-wide tree total.
[chapter-p004] Planting start of proposed response; young trees need watering and maintenance before substantial shade, some sites cannot accommodate roots. Temporary shade structures proposed at those sites while planners investigate longer-term options; not recommendation to replace existing mature trees with structures. Report warned that choosing one fast-growing species everywhere leaves whole planting program vulnerable to same pest.
[chapter-p005] Authors described findings as initial local comparison, not forecast; had not measured winter conditions, unusually humid days, indoor temperatures, or health outcomes. Proposed repeating measurements in another summer and including observations of how people used shaded routes; even if later measurements confirm cooler air, whether particular intervention improves residents' daily experience would still depend on access, maintenance, and where shade fell.
episodes.summary:
* Twelve streets with mature trees measured against twelve without; shaded streets cooler on average, but difference largest late afternoon.
* Shade reduces pavement and people's sunlight absorption; trees release water vapor through leaves, cooling surrounding air.
* Tree cover unevenly distributed; older residential streets wider planting strips, hottest blocks contained busiest bus stops.
* Planting start of proposed response; young trees need watering and maintenance before substantial shade, some sites cannot accommodate roots.
* Authors described findings as initial local comparison, not forecast; whether particular intervention improves residents' daily experience would still depend on access, maintenance, and where shade fell.
